spec.name: Singly Linked List Module
spec.description: A Python module (linked_list.py) providing a singly linked list class `LinkedList` (with an internal `Node` class) that supports insert, delete, search, and reverse operations, plus a pytest test suite (test_linked_list.py) covering every method, including edge and error cases. Design decisions: values may be any Python object compared with ==; `insert(value, index=None)` appends to the tail when index is None, otherwise inserts before the given position (0 = head, len = tail); an out-of-range or non-integer index raises IndexError / TypeError respectively; `delete(value)` removes the first node whose value equals the argument and returns True, or returns False if not found (no exception); `search(value)` returns the zero-based index of the first match or -1 if absent; `reverse()` reverses the list in place and returns None. The class also supports len(), iteration, and `to_list()` to make behaviour testable.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new LinkedList() is empty: len() is 0, to_list() returns [], and iterating yields nothing.
insert(value) with no index appends the value at the tail; inserting 1, 2, 3 in order gives to_list() == [1, 2, 3] and len() == 3.

insert(value, index) inserts the value so it ends up at that position: index 0 inserts at the head, index == len(list) inserts at the tail, and a middle index inserts between existing nodes, preserving the order of other elements.
insert with an index that is negative or greater than len(list) raises IndexError and leaves the list unchanged; a non-integer index (e.g. 'a' or 1.5) raises TypeError.

delete(value) removes the first node equal to value and returns True; it works for head, middle, and tail nodes and for a single-element list, and len() decreases by 1; when duplicates exist only the first occurrence is removed.
delete(value) on an empty list or with a value not present returns False and leaves the list unchanged.
search(value) returns the zero-based index of the first node equal to value, or -1 if the value is not present (including on an empty list).

reverse() reverses the list in place so to_list() returns the elements in the opposite order, and returns None; it works for lists of length 0, 1, 2 and many; after reversing, insert (append), delete, and search operate correctly on the new order (tail is updated correctly).
The module provides __len__ and __iter__ (and to_list()) that always reflect the current state after any sequence of insert, delete and reverse operations.
A pytest test file exercises every public method (insert, delete, search, reverse, len, iteration, to_list) including the success, edge and error cases above, and all tests pass.

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"


# ===== test_linked_list.py =====
from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():
    assert len(LinkedList()) == 0


def test_empty_head_is_none():
    assert LinkedList().head is None


def test_empty_to_list():
    assert LinkedList().to_list() == []


def test_empty_iter():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():
    assert not LinkedList()


def test_empty_consistent():
    assert_consistent(LinkedList())


def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
    ll._size = 3
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert ll
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_iter_yields_values_not_nodes():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    assert all(not isinstance(v, Node) for v in ll)


def test_iterating_twice_gives_same_result():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    assert list(ll) == list(ll)
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]


def test_to_list_returns_new_list_each_call():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    a = ll.to_list()
    b = ll.to_list()
    assert a == b and a is not b
    a.append(99)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]


def test_reprs():
    assert repr(LinkedList()) == "LinkedList([])"
    assert repr(make_list([1, "a"])) == "LinkedList([1, 'a'])"
    assert repr(Node(3)) == "Node(3)"


def test_falsy_values_round_trip_and_list_truthy():
    for v in (0, None, "", False):
        ll = make_list([v])
        assert len(ll) == 1
        assert ll
        assert ll.to_list() == [v]
    ll = make_list([None, 0, None])
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, None]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_assert_consistent_detects_mismatch():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll._size = 5
    try:
        assert_consistent(ll)
    except AssertionError:
        return
    raise RuntimeError("helper failed to detect size mismatch")

Self-review:
- [edge_case] LinkedList._size / __len__: Size is a separate counter that the later tasks (insert, delete, reverse) must keep in sync with the chain of nodes. Nothing checks this now. If a later task forgets to update `_size`, `len()` and `to_list()` will disagree and the empty-list tests won't catch it. Also, because `head` is public, a caller can change the chain without updating `_size`. → Add a test helper that asserts `len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())`. Call it after every mutation in the T2–T5 tests. Add a note in the docstring that `_size` must be updated by every mutator.
- [edge_case] LinkedList.__iter__: The iterator is a generator that walks live nodes. If the list is mutated during iteration (for example, `delete` inside a `for` loop), it silently skips or repeats items. If the chain has a cycle, `to_list()` never ends and uses unbounded memory. Neither behavior is documented or tested. → Document that mutating during iteration is unsupported. Optionally add a test that iterating twice over the same list gives the same result: `assert list(ll) == list(ll)`.
- [edge_case] test_linked_list.py (coverage): The tests only cover the empty list. Iteration order and `to_list` are not exercised on a non-empty list. # ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int (bool is rejected too) and
        IndexError if it is outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left
        unchanged when an error is raised.
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                prev = prev.next
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1


# ===== test_linked_list.py =====
import pytest

from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():
    assert len(LinkedList()) == 0


def test_empty_head_is_none():
    assert LinkedList().head is None


def test_empty_to_list():
    assert LinkedList().to_list() == []


def test_empty_iter():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():
    assert not LinkedList()


def test_empty_consistent():
    assert_consistent(LinkedList())


def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
    ll._size = 3
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert ll
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_iter_yields_values_not_nodes():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    assert all(not isinstance(v, Node) for v in ll)


def test_iterating_twice_gives_same_result():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    assert list(ll) == list(ll)
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]


def test_to_list_returns_new_list_each_call():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    a = ll.to_list()
    b = ll.to_list()
    assert a == b and a is not b
    a.append(99)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]


def test_reprs():
    assert repr(LinkedList()) == "LinkedList([])"
    assert repr(make_list([1, "a"])) == "LinkedList([1, 'a'])"
    assert repr(Node(3)) == "Node(3)"


def test_falsy_values_round_trip_and_list_truthy():
    for v in (0, None, "", False):
        ll = make_list([v])
        assert len(ll) == 1
        assert ll
        assert ll.to_list() == [v]
    ll = make_list([None, 0, None])
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, None]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_assert_consistent_detects_mismatch():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll._size = 5
    try:
        assert_consistent(ll)
    except AssertionError:
        return
    raise RuntimeError("helper failed to detect size mismatch")


# ---- insert ----

def test_append_returns_none_and_orders():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert ll.insert(1) is None
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(3)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_into_empty_at_zero():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.insert("x", 0)
    assert ll.to_list() == ["x"]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_at_head():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll.insert(0, 0)
    assert ll.to_list() == [0, 1, 2]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_middle():
    ll = make_list([1, 3])
    ll.insert(2, 1)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_at_len_is_tail():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll.insert(3, 2)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    ll.insert(4)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3, 4]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_tail_then_append_keeps_chain_intact():
    ll = LinkedList()
    for i in range(5):
        ll.insert(i, len(ll))
    ll.insert(99, 2)
    assert ll.to_list() == [0, 1, 99, 2, 3, 4]
    assert_consistent(ll)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [-1, -100, 4, 10])
def test_out_of_range_index_raises_and_leaves_list_unchanged(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        ll.insert(9, bad)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_out_of_range_on_empty_list():
    ll = LinkedList()
    for bad in (1, -1):
        with pytest.raises(IndexError):
            ll.insert(1, bad)
    assert ll.to_list() == []
    assert ll.head is None
    assert_consistent(ll)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", ["a", 1.5, 1.0, [0], (0,), True, False])
def test_non_integer_index_raises_type_error(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        ll.insert(9, bad)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_arbitrary_objects_including_falsy():
    ll = LinkedList()
    obj = object()
    for v in (None, 0, "", obj, [1]):
        ll.insert(v)
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, "", obj, [1]]
    assert len(ll) == 5
    assert_consistent(ll)

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():
    assert len(LinkedList()) == 0


def test_empty_head_is_none():
    assert LinkedList().head is None


def test_empty_to_list():
    assert LinkedList().to_list() == []


def test_empty_iter():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():
    assert not LinkedList()


def test_empty_consistent():
    assert_consistent(LinkedList())


def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
    ll._size = 3
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert ll
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_iter_yields_values_not_nodes():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    assert all(not isinstance(v, Node) for v in ll)


def test_iterating_twice_gives_same_result():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    assert list(ll) == list(ll)
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]


def test_to_list_returns_new_list_each_call():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    a = ll.to_list()
    b = ll.to_list()
    assert a == b and a is not b
    a.append(99)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]


def test_reprs():
    assert repr(LinkedList()) == "LinkedList([])"
    assert repr(make_list([1, "a"])) == "LinkedList([1, 'a'])"
    assert repr(Node(3)) == "Node(3)"


def test_falsy_values_round_trip_and_list_truthy():
    for v in (0, None, "", False):
        ll = make_list([v])
        assert len(ll) == 1
        assert ll
        assert ll.to_list() == [v]
    ll = make_list([None, 0, None])
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, None]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_assert_consistent_detects_mismatch():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll._size = 5
    try:
        assert_consistent(ll)
    except AssertionError:
        return
    raise RuntimeError("helper failed to detect size mismatch")


# ---- insert ----

def test_append_returns_none_and_orders():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert ll.insert(1) is None
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(3)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_into_empty_at_zero():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.insert("x", 0)
    assert ll.to_list() == ["x"]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_at_head():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll.insert(0, 0)
    assert ll.to_list() == [0, 1, 2]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_middle():
    ll = make_list([1, 3])
    ll.insert(2, 1)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_at_len_is_tail():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll.insert(3, 2)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    ll.insert(4)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3, 4]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_tail_then_append_keeps_chain_intact():
    ll = LinkedList()
    for i in range(5):
        ll.insert(i, len(ll))
    ll.insert(99, 2)
    assert ll.to_list() == [0, 1, 99, 2, 3, 4]
    assert_consistent(ll)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [-1, -100, 4, 10, 10**100, -(10**100)])
def test_out_of_range_index_raises_and_leaves_list_unchanged(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    old_head, old_size = ll.head, len(ll)
    old_nodes = [ll.head, ll.head.next, ll.head.next.next]
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        ll.insert(9, bad)
    assert ll.head is old_head
    assert ll._size == old_size
    assert [ll.head, ll.head.next, ll.head.next.next] == old_nodes
    assert ll.head.next.next.next is None
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_out_of_range_on_empty_list():
    ll = LinkedList()
    for bad in (1, -1):
        with pytest.raises(IndexError):
            ll.insert(1, bad)
    assert ll.to_list() == []
    assert ll.head is None
    assert_consistent(ll)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad", ["a", "0", 1.5, 1.0, [0], (0,), True, False, Decimal(1), b"1"]
)
def test_non_integer_index_raises_type_error(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    old_head, old_size = ll.head, len(ll)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        ll.insert(9, bad)
    assert ll.head is old_head
    assert ll._size == old_size
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]
    assert_consistent(ll)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [False, True, "0", 0.0])
def test_non_integer_index_on_empty_list_raises_and_leaves_it_empty(bad):
    ll = LinkedList()
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        ll.insert(1, bad)
    assert ll.head is None
    assert len(ll) == 0
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_index_like_objects_are_rejected():
    class Idx:
        def __index__(self):
            return 0

    ll = make_list([1])
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        ll.insert(2, Idx())
    assert ll.to_list() == [1]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_error_messages_mention_problem():
    ll = make_list([1])
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="str"):
        ll.insert(2, "a")
    with pytest.raises(IndexError, match="out of range"):
        ll.insert(2, 5)


def test_insert_at_len_works_on_hand_built_list():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    ll.insert("x", len(ll))
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3, "x"]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_size_chain_mismatch_gives_clear_failure():
    ll = make_list([1])
    ll._size = 5  # corrupt invariant on purpose
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="mismatch"):
        ll.insert(2, 5)


def test_many_appends():
    ll = LinkedList()
    n = 3000
    for i in range(n):
        ll.insert(i)
    assert len(ll) == n
    values = ll.to_list()
    assert values[-1] == n - 1
    assert values == list(range(n))
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_arbitrary_objects_including_falsy():
    ll = LinkedList()
    obj = object()
    for v in (None, 0, "", obj, [1]):
        ll.insert(v)
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, "", obj, [1]]
    assert len(ll) == 5
    assert_consistent(ll)
result.explanation:
I addressed all five review items with code changes or new tests. test_linked_list.py passes with 48 tests and test_qa_t1.py passes with 15, each run with exec_python.

- **Index type:** I kept the strict `int` check, so `bool` and objects with `__index__` (such as numpy integers) still raise TypeError. The `insert` docstring now says so, and a test covers a small class with `__index__`.
- **Size/chain mismatch:** I added `assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"` in the walk loop. A test shows a corrupted `_size` now fails with that message. Another test checks that `insert(x, len(ll))` works on a hand-built list.
- **Append speed:** I did not add a tail pointer. `head` is public and the tests build lists by hand, so a tail pointer could go out of sync. The docstring now says every insert is O(n). A test appends 3000 items and checks the length and last value. I used 3000 rather than the suggested 10,000 so the test stays fast.
- **Failed inserts leave the chain untouched:** the error tests now check that `head` is the same object, that `_size` is unchanged, and that the node objects themselves are unchanged. The IndexError cases also include `10**100` and `-10**100`.
- **Non-int indexes:** I added `'0'`, `Decimal(1)` and `b'1'` to the TypeError cases. I also added a test that inserting with `False`, `True`, `'0'` or `0.0` into an empty list raises TypeError and leaves the list empty. A further test checks the error-message text.
plan: Document strict int index and O(n) insert; add clear assertion on size/chain mismatch
Strengthen error tests (head identity, huge indexes, empty-list bool, '0', Decimal, __index__ objects) and add bulk append test

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node whose value == ``value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). Values are
        compared with ``==`` (``node.value == value``); the list is not modified.
        """
        index = 0
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            if node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
            index += 1
        return -1


# ===== test_linked_list.py =====
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():
    assert len(LinkedList()) == 0


def test_empty_head_is_none():
    assert LinkedList().head is None


def test_empty_to_list():
    assert LinkedList().to_list() == []


def test_empty_iter():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():
    assert not LinkedList()


def test_empty_consistent():
    assert_consistent(LinkedList())


def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
    ll._size = 3
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert ll
    assert_consistent(ll)

"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node whose value == ``value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). Values are
        compared with ``==`` (``node.value == value``); the list is not modified.
        """
        index = 0
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            if node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
            index += 1
        return -1

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node matching ``value``.

        A node matches if ``node.value is value`` or ``node.value == value``
        (identity first, like ``list.index``), so a NaN object stored in the
        list is found when searched for by that same object, while a different
        NaN object is not. The comparison is evaluated as
        ``node.value == value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). The list is
        never modified. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate to the caller.

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain, so an accidental cycle created by editing
        ``next`` directly cannot make ``search`` loop forever.
        """
        node = self.head
        for index in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
        return -1

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():
    assert len(LinkedList()) == 0


def test_empty_head_is_none():
    assert LinkedList().head is None


def test_empty_to_list():
    assert LinkedList().to_list() == []


def test_empty_iter():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():
    assert not LinkedList()


def test_empty_consistent():
    assert_consistent(LinkedList())


def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
    ll._size = 3
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert ll
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_iter_yields_values_not_nodes():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    assert all(not isinstance(v, Node) for v in ll)


def test_iterating_twice_gives_same_result():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    assert list(ll) == list(ll)
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]


def test_to_list_returns_new_list_each_call():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    a = ll.to_list()
    b = ll.to_list()
    assert a == b and a is not b
    a.append(99)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]


def test_reprs():
    assert repr(LinkedList()) == "LinkedList([])"
    assert repr(make_list([1, "a"])) == "LinkedList([1, 'a'])"
    assert repr(Node(3)) == "Node(3)"


def test_falsy_values_round_trip_and_list_truthy():
    for v in (0, None, "", False):
        ll = make_list([v])
        assert len(ll) == 1
        assert ll
        assert ll.to_list() == [v]
    ll = make_list([None, 0, None])
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, None]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_assert_consistent_detects_mismatch():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll._size = 5
    try:

    except AssertionError:

    raise RuntimeError("helper failed to detect size mismatch")

def test_append_returns_none_and_orders():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert ll.insert(1) is None
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(3)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3

def test_insert_into_empty_at_zero():

    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_at_head():

def test_insert_middle():

    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)

    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    ll.insert(4)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3, 4]

def test_out_of_range_index_raises_and_leaves_list_unchanged(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])

    assert ll.to_list() == []
    assert ll.head is None
    assert_consistent(ll)

    with pytest.raises(TypeError):

    assert ll.head is None
    assert len(ll) == 0
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_index_like_objects_are_rejected():
    class Idx:

    ll = make_list([1])
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):

    with pytest.raises(IndexError, match="out of range"):

    assert len(ll) == 5
    assert_consistent(ll)

    ll = make_list([10, 20, 30, 40])
    assert ll.search(10) == 0
    assert ll.search(30) == 2
    assert ll.search(40) == 3
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_search_single_element():

def test_search_returns_first_duplicate():

def test_search_missing_and_empty():

    class Eq:

        (identity first, like ``list.index``), so a NaN object stored in the
        list is found when searched for by that same object, while a different
        NaN object is not. The comparison is evaluated as
        ``node.value == value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). The list is
        never modified. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate to the caller.

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain, so an accidental cycle created by editing
        ``next`` directly cannot make ``search`` loop forever.
        """
        node = self.head
        for index in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
        return -1

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():

def test_empty_head_is_none():

def test_empty_to_list():

def test_empty_iter():

    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():

def test_empty_consistent():

def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))

Self-review:
- [edge_case] linked_list.py: LinkedList.insert, type check (`isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int)`): Integer-like objects that implement `__index__`, such as `numpy.int64`, are rejected with TypeError even though they are valid positions. `operator.index` would accept them. The spec only says non-int raises TypeError, so rejecting them is defensible. But the choice is not documented or tested, and a caller passing an index computed by numpy gets a surprising error. → Either keep the strict check and add a docstring line and a test saying that only real `int` (not bool) is accepted. Or switch to `operator.index(index)` inside try/except TypeError, keep the explicit bool rejection, and add a test for a small class with `__index__`.
- [bug] linked_list.py: LinkedList.insert, positional walk (`prev = prev.next` loop): The walk trusts `_size` to match the chain. `head` and `_size` are public or semi-public and the tests set them by hand. If they disagree, for example `_size` is larger than the real chain, then `prev` becomes None. The result is an opaque `AttributeError: 'NoneType' has no attribute 'next'`, and a partially applied change is possible. The range check passes because it only looks at `_size`. → Do not add defensive code in production. Add a test that documents the invariant, for example that `make_list` produces a list where `insert(x, len(ll))` works. Optionally, in the loop, `assert prev is not None, 'size/chain mismatch'` to give a clearer failure.
- [edge_case] linked_list.py: LinkedList.insert, append path (index=None → index = self._size): Every append walks the whole list, so building a list of n items is O(n²). No tail pointer is kept. This is correct but slow for large lists. It also means other methods (delete and reverse in later tasks) must keep any future tail pointer in sync. For now the only risk is performance. → Add a `_tail` reference updated in insert, delete and reverse, to make append O(1). Or accept O(n) and note it in the docstring. A future implementation could relink nodes and then raise, and `to_list` could still look the same. Very large indexes (`10**100`), `None` passed through a variable, and error message content are also not covered. → In the error tests, capture `old_head = ll.head` and `old_size = len(ll)` before the call. # ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node matching ``value``.

        A node matches if ``node.value is value`` or ``node.value == value``
        (identity first, like ``list.index``), so a NaN object stored in the
        list is found when searched for by that same object, while a different
        NaN object is not. The comparison is evaluated as
        ``node.value == value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). The list is
        never modified. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate to the caller.

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain, so an accidental cycle created by editing
        ``next`` directly cannot make ``search`` loop forever.
        """
        node = self.head
        for index in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
        return -1

    def delete(self, value):
        """Remove the first node matching ``value``; return True if removed.

        Matching is the same as in ``search`` (``node.value is value`` or
        ``node.value == value``). Returns False, leaving the list unchanged,
        if nothing matches (including on an empty list); no exception is
        raised for a missing value. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate and
        leave the list unchanged, since unlinking happens only after a match.

        Only the first match is removed. ``_size`` is decremented on success.
        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` so a cycle cannot hang it.
        """
        prev = None
        node = self.head
        for _ in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                if prev is None:
                    self.head = node.next
                else:
                    prev.next = node.next
                node.next = None
                self._size -= 1
                return True
            prev = node
            node = node.next
        return False

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():
    assert len(LinkedList()) == 0


def test_empty_head_is_none():
    assert LinkedList().head is None


def test_empty_to_list():
    assert LinkedList().to_list() == []


def test_empty_iter():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():
    assert not LinkedList()


def test_empty_consistent():
    assert_consistent(LinkedList())


def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
    ll._size = 3
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert ll
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_iter_yields_values_not_nodes():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    assert all(not isinstance(v, Node) for v in ll)


def test_iterating_twice_gives_same_result():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    assert list(ll) == list(ll)
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]


def test_to_list_returns_new_list_each_call():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    a = ll.to_list()
    b = ll.to_list()
    assert a == b and a is not b
    a.append(99)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]


def test_reprs():
    assert repr(LinkedList()) == "LinkedList([])"
    assert repr(make_list([1, "a"])) == "LinkedList([1, 'a'])"
    assert repr(Node(3)) == "Node(3)"


def test_falsy_values_round_trip_and_list_truthy():
    for v in (0, None, "", False):
        ll = make_list([v])
        assert len(ll) == 1
        assert ll
        assert ll.to_list() == [v]
    ll = make_list([None, 0, None])
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, None]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_assert_consistent_detects_mismatch():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll._size = 5
    try:
        assert_consistent(ll)
    except AssertionError:
        return
    raise RuntimeError("helper failed to detect size mismatch")

    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]

def test_insert_at_len_is_tail():

@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [-1, -100, 4, 10, 10**100, -(10**100)])
def test_out_of_range_index_raises_and_leaves_list_unchanged(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    old_head, old_size = ll.head, len(ll)
    old_nodes = [ll.head, ll.head.next, ll.head.next.next]

    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)

"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node matching ``value``.

        A node matches if ``node.value is value`` or ``node.value == value``
        (identity first, like ``list.index``), so a NaN object stored in the
        list is found when searched for by that same object, while a different
        NaN object is not. The comparison is evaluated as
        ``node.value == value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). The list is
        never modified. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate to the caller.

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain, so an accidental cycle created by editing
        ``next`` directly cannot make ``search`` loop forever.
        """
        node = self.head
        for index in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
        return -1

    def delete(self, value):
        """Remove the first node matching ``value``; return True if removed.

        Matching is the same as in ``search`` (``node.value is value`` or
        ``node.value == value``). Returns False, leaving the list unchanged,
        if nothing matches (including on an empty list); no exception is
        raised for a missing value. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate and
        leave the list unchanged, since unlinking happens only after a match.

        Only the first match is removed. ``_size`` is decremented on success.
        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` so a cycle cannot hang it.
        """
        prev = None
        node = self.head
        for _ in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                if prev is None:
                    self.head = node.next
                else:
                    prev.next = node.next
                node.next = None
                self._size -= 1
                return True
            prev = node
            node = node.next
        return False

# ===== linked_list.py =====
"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node matching ``value``.

        A node matches if ``node.value is value`` or ``node.value == value``
        (identity first, like ``list.index``), so a NaN object stored in the
        list is found when searched for by that same object, while a different
        NaN object is not. The comparison is evaluated as
        ``node.value == value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). The list is
        never modified. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate to the caller.

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain, so an accidental cycle created by editing
        ``next`` directly cannot make ``search`` loop forever.
        """
        node = self.head
        for index in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
        return -1

    def delete(self, value):
        """Remove the first node matching ``value``; return True if removed.

        Matching is the same as in ``search`` (``node.value is value`` or
        ``node.value == value``). Returns False, leaving the list unchanged,
        if nothing matches (including on an empty list); no exception is
        raised for a missing value. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate and
        leave the list unchanged, since unlinking happens only after a match.

        Only the first match is removed. ``_size`` is decremented on success.

        The removed node's own ``next`` is deliberately left intact, so
        deleting the current item inside ``for v in ll`` does not end the
        iteration early (the iterator resumes from the removed node and
        carries on with its successor).

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain. A cycle therefore cannot hang it, but on a
        cyclic chain the resulting structure is undefined beyond that, and if
        ``_size`` is too small a node beyond that point is not found
        (returns False).
        """
        prev = None
        node = self.head
        for _ in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                if prev is None:
                    self.head = node.next
                else:
                    prev.next = node.next
                self._size -= 1
                return True
            prev = node
            node = node.next
        return False


# ===== test_linked_list.py =====
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from linked_list import LinkedList, Node


def assert_consistent(ll):
    """Check that the size counter agrees with the actual node chain.

    Call after every mutation in tests.
    """
    count = 0
    node = ll.head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    assert len(ll) == count
    assert len(ll) == len(ll.to_list())


def make_list(values):
    """Build a LinkedList by hand (independent of insert)."""
    ll = LinkedList()
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = Node(v, head)
    ll.head = head
    ll._size = len(values)
    return ll


def test_imports():
    assert Node is not None and LinkedList is not None


def test_node_attributes():
    n = Node(5)
    assert n.value == 5
    assert n.next is None
    m = Node(1, n)
    assert m.next is n


def test_empty_len():
    assert len(LinkedList()) == 0


def test_empty_head_is_none():
    assert LinkedList().head is None


def test_empty_to_list():
    assert LinkedList().to_list() == []


def test_empty_iter():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert list(iter(ll)) == []
    assert list(ll) == []


def test_empty_is_falsy():
    assert not LinkedList()


def test_empty_consistent():
    assert_consistent(LinkedList())


def test_manual_nodes_non_empty():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.head = Node(1, Node(2, Node(3)))
    ll._size = 3
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert ll
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_iter_yields_values_not_nodes():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    assert all(not isinstance(v, Node) for v in ll)


def test_iterating_twice_gives_same_result():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    assert list(ll) == list(ll)
    assert list(ll) == [1, 2, 3]


def test_to_list_returns_new_list_each_call():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    a = ll.to_list()
    b = ll.to_list()
    assert a == b and a is not b
    a.append(99)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]


def test_reprs():
    assert repr(LinkedList()) == "LinkedList([])"
    assert repr(make_list([1, "a"])) == "LinkedList([1, 'a'])"
    assert repr(Node(3)) == "Node(3)"


def test_falsy_values_round_trip_and_list_truthy():
    for v in (0, None, "", False):
        ll = make_list([v])
        assert len(ll) == 1
        assert ll
        assert ll.to_list() == [v]
    ll = make_list([None, 0, None])
    assert ll.to_list() == [None, 0, None]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_assert_consistent_detects_mismatch():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll._size = 5
    try:
        assert_consistent(ll)
    except AssertionError:
        return
    raise RuntimeError("helper failed to detect size mismatch")


# ---- insert ----

def test_append_returns_none_and_orders():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert ll.insert(1) is None
    ll.insert(2)
    ll.insert(3)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert len(ll) == 3
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_into_empty_at_zero():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.insert("x", 0)
    assert ll.to_list() == ["x"]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_at_head():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll.insert(0, 0)
    assert ll.to_list() == [0, 1, 2]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_middle():
    ll = make_list([1, 3])
    ll.insert(2, 1)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_at_len_is_tail():
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    ll.insert(3, 2)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    ll.insert(4)
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3, 4]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_insert_tail_then_append_keeps_chain_intact():
    ll = LinkedList()
    for i in range(5):
        ll.insert(i, len(ll))
    ll.insert(99, 2)
    assert ll.to_list() == [0, 1, 99, 2, 3, 4]
    assert_consistent(ll)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [-1, -100, 4, 10, 10**100, -(10**100)])
def test_out_of_range_index_raises_and_leaves_list_unchanged(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    old_head, old_size = ll.head, len(ll)
    old_nodes = [ll.head, ll.head.next, ll.head.next.next]
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        ll.insert(9, bad)
    assert ll.head is old_head
    assert ll._size == old_size
    assert [ll.head, ll.head.next, ll.head.next.next] == old_nodes
    assert ll.head.next.next.next is None
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_out_of_range_on_empty_list():
    ll = LinkedList()
    for bad in (1, -1):
        with pytest.raises(IndexError):
            ll.insert(1, bad)
    assert ll.to_list() == []
    assert ll.head is None
    assert_consistent(ll)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad", ["a", "0", 1.5, 1.0, [0], (0,), True, False, Decimal(1), b"1"]
)
def test_non_integer_index_raises_type_error(bad):
    ll = make_list([1, 2])
    old_head, old_size = ll.head, len(ll)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        ll.insert(9, bad)
    assert ll.head is old_head
    assert ll._size == old_size
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2]
    assert_consistent(ll)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [False, True, "0", 0.0])
def test_non_integer_index_on_empty_list_raises_and_leaves_it_empty(bad):
    ll = LinkedList()
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        ll.insert(1, bad)
    assert ll.head is None
    assert len(ll) == 0
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_index_like_objects_are_rejected():
    class Idx:
        def __index__(self):
            return 0

    ll = make_list([1])
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        ll.insert(2, Idx())
    assert ll.to_list() == [1]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_error_messages_mention_problem():
    ll = make_list([1])
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="str"):
        ll.insert(2, "a")
    with pytest.raises(IndexError, match="out of range"):
        ll.insert(2, 5)


def test_insert_at_len_works_on_hand_built_list():
    ll = make_list([1, 2, 3])
    ll.insert("x", len(ll))
    assert ll.to_list() == [1, 2, 3, "x"]
    assert_consistent(ll)


def test_size_chain_mismatch_gives_clear_failure():

I addressed all five review items. test_linked_list.py passes with 87 tests and test_qa_t1.py passes with 15, each run with exec_python.

- **Delete during iteration:** I removed `node.next = None` from `delete`. Deleting the current item inside `for v in ll` no longer ends the loop early. A new test deletes the even values while iterating and checks every item is still seen. The docstring explains this.
- **Stale `_size`:** the delete docstring now says the walk is bounded by `_size`. A test sets `_size = 2` on a 3-node list and checks `delete(3)` returns False and leaves the list unchanged.
- **Cyclic list:** the docstring now says that on a cycle `delete` only promises to terminate, and the resulting structure is undefined. A new test deletes each present value of a cyclic list, checking it returns True and `_size` drops by 1.
- **`==` returning a non-bool:** a test uses an `__eq__` whose result raises ValueError when tested for truth. It checks `delete` raises and leaves the list unchanged.
- **Identity versus equality and operand order:**
  - One test checks the first equal node is removed even when a later node is the identical object.
  - One checks an object whose `__eq__` always returns False is still deleted by passing the same object.
  - One checks the comparison is called as `node.value == value`.

"""Singly linked list module."""


class Node:
    """A single node holding a value and a reference to the next node.

    The ``next`` parameter name mirrors the attribute; it shadows the builtin
    only inside ``__init__``, which is harmless.
    """

    def __init__(self, value, next=None):
        self.value = value
        self.next = next

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Node({self.value!r})"


class LinkedList:
    """A singly linked list.

    Invariant: ``_size`` always equals the number of nodes reachable from
    ``head``. Every mutating method (insert, delete, reverse, ...) must keep
    ``_size`` in sync. Code that edits ``head``/``next`` directly must update
    ``_size`` itself.

    Mutating the list while iterating over it is unsupported; the iterator
    walks live nodes, so items may be skipped or repeated. The chain must not
    contain a cycle, or iteration will never finish.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = None
        self._size = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self._size

    def __iter__(self):
        node = self.head
        while node is not None:
            yield node.value
            node = node.next

    def to_list(self):
        """Return the values as a new regular Python list on each call."""
        return list(self)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"LinkedList({self.to_list()!r})"

    def insert(self, value, index=None):
        """Insert ``value``.

        With ``index=None`` the value is appended at the tail. Otherwise it is
        inserted before the node currently at ``index`` (0 = head,
        ``len(self)`` = tail).

        Only a real ``int`` is accepted as an index: ``bool`` and objects that
        merely implement ``__index__`` (e.g. numpy integers) are rejected with
        TypeError; convert with ``int(...)`` first.

        Raises TypeError if ``index`` is not an int and IndexError if it is
        outside ``0..len(self)``. The list is left unchanged when an error is
        raised.

        Performance: no tail pointer is kept (``head`` is public and may be
        edited directly), so every insert, including an append, is O(n).
        """
        if index is None:
            index = self._size
        elif isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
            raise TypeError(
                f"index must be an int or None, not {type(index).__name__}"
            )
        elif index < 0 or index > self._size:
            raise IndexError(f"index {index} out of range 0..{self._size}")

        if index == 0:
            self.head = Node(value, self.head)
        else:
            prev = self.head
            for _ in range(index - 1):
                assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
                prev = prev.next
            assert prev is not None, "size/chain mismatch"
            prev.next = Node(value, prev.next)
        self._size += 1

    def search(self, value):
        """Return the zero-based index of the first node matching ``value``.

        A node matches if ``node.value is value`` or ``node.value == value``
        (identity first, like ``list.index``), so a NaN object stored in the
        list is found when searched for by that same object, while a different
        NaN object is not. The comparison is evaluated as
        ``node.value == value``.

        Returns -1 if no node matches (including on an empty list). The list is
        never modified. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate to the caller.

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain, so an accidental cycle created by editing
        ``next`` directly cannot make ``search`` loop forever.
        """
        node = self.head
        for index in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                return index
            node = node.next
        return -1

    def delete(self, value):
        """Remove the first node matching ``value``; return True if removed.

        Matching is the same as in ``search`` (``node.value is value`` or
        ``node.value == value``). Returns False, leaving the list unchanged,
        if nothing matches (including on an empty list); no exception is
        raised for a missing value. Exceptions raised by ``==`` propagate and
        leave the list unchanged, since unlinking happens only after a match.

        Only the first match is removed. ``_size`` is decremented on success.

        The removed node's own ``next`` is deliberately left intact, so
        deleting the current item inside ``for v in ll`` does not end the
        iteration early (the iterator resumes from the removed node and
        carries on with its successor).

        The walk is bounded by ``len(self)`` (the ``_size`` invariant) as well
        as by the end of the chain. A cycle therefore cannot hang it, but on a
        cyclic chain the resulting structure is undefined beyond that, and if
        ``_size`` is too small a node beyond that point is not found
        (returns False).
        """
        prev = None
        node = self.head
        for _ in range(self._size):
            if node is None:
                break
            if node.value is value or node.value == value:
                if prev is None:
                    self.head = node.next
                else:
                    prev.next = node.next
                self._size -= 1
                return True
            prev = node
            node = node.next
        return False
